correctness.rationale: Invariance of the second coordinate gives the exact marginal identity \(y_\#\mu=(bx)_\#\mu\). Invariance of the first coordinate then gives \(a\mathbb E[x^2]+(1-b)\mathbb E[x]-1=0\). Factoring the fixed-point polynomial and applying Vieta yields the variance parabola exactly. Endpoint equality forces zero variance and hence the corresponding fixed-point atom. For the strip statement, zero pointwise fixed-point polynomial on the invariant support implies that current and previous \(x\)-coordinates are roots; the update becomes a strict convex combination unless they agree, so the support reduces to the two fixed points. Otherwise zero mean of the continuous fixed-point polynomial forces both signs on sets of positive measure. The packaged exact checker verifies the stationary algebra and the classical radical fixed-point arithmetic.

The full open Senti–Takahasi preprint explicitly works with the space of all invariant Borel probability measures and thermodynamic formalism at the first bifurcation; targeted searches of the inspected text found no moment, average, variance-parabola, or strip-crossing statement. The classical rigorous Hénon literature on hyperbolicity and Sinai–Bowen–Ruelle measures is highly relevant context but no inspected source or targeted same-object search supplied an implication of the accepted theorem. The closest indexed mathematical result found is an analogous variance-gap theorem for a different continuous-time system.

value.rationale: The Hénon map is a canonical benchmark for strange attractors, periodic-orbit theory, Sinai–Bowen–Ruelle measures, and thermodynamic formalism. The accepted theorem compresses the first two stationary moments of every compact invariant measure to a single exact parabola whose endpoints are the map’s two fixed points. More importantly, the zero-mean fixed-point polynomial gives a geometric recurrence obstruction: no genuinely non-fixed invariant measure can live entirely inside the vertical strip between the fixed points or entirely outside it; it must assign positive mass to both regions. The statement applies at once to periodic-orbit measures and chaotic measures and supplies a parameter-explicit exact consistency test for numerical invariant-measure or periodic-orbit computations. This is a natural structural constraint tied directly to the canonical fixed-point geometry, not an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of a tabulated statistic.
